papers.title: Dataset Fragmentation, Cognitive Variability, and Reproducibility Challenges in EEG-Based Brain-Computer Interfaces: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review.
papers.summary: A PRISMA-based systematic mapping review of 16,920 records (129 retained publications) examined whether heterogeneous public EEG-BCI datasets can support reproducible cross-dataset analysis. It identified fragmentation across acquisition, channel layouts, task/event semantics, preprocessing, participant context, and evaluation, with median reporting transparency of 9/10, data availability in 61.2%, and code/pipeline availability in 20.9%, concluding that scalable cross-dataset analysis requires compatibility rules, provenance, contextual metadata, and auditable transformations.

papers.title: The Deep-Match Framework for Event-Related Potential Detection in EEG.
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study evaluated the Deep-Match framework for single-trial event-related potential detection in multi-channel EEG during laser stimulation, comparing a standard randomly initialized deep model, an ERP-template-initialized Deep-MF model, and a matched filter detector under leave-one-out validation. Neural network models outperformed the matched filter, and Deep-MF slightly exceeded the standard model for most held-out subjects, with higher average F1-score (0.37 vs. 0.34) and best F1-score 0.71 versus 0.59 despite substantial inter-subject variability.

papers.title: EEG Subject Identification and Open-Set Rejection Across Paradigms.
papers.summary: Compared EEG-based subject identification and open-set rejection across five paradigms (resting state, transient and steady-state sensory stimulation, P300 Oddball, motor execution) using the M3CV database. Transient sensory stimulation yielded the highest within-session Rank-1 accuracy (98.10%) and open-set performance (AU-OSCR 97.36%), but cross-session transfer degraded severely (Rank-1 ~1.9-5.4%), showing strong session dependence.

papers.title: Subject Identity Confounds qEEG Emotion Recognition on DEAP and DREAMER.
papers.summary: Re-evaluated qEEG-based valence and arousal recognition on DEAP and DREAMER under trial-grouped, participant-independent, within-participant, and cross-dataset protocols. Epoch-pooled AUCs (0.689 valence, 0.711 arousal) dropped to near-chance under participant-independent evaluation (0.493, 0.447), while the same features identified participants with up to 0.998 accuracy, indicating that pooled emotion scores largely reflect participant-specific recording structure.

papers.title: Pre-movement sensor-level EEG activity recorded with a portable three-channel system is associated with futsal free-kick outcomes
papers.summary: Tested whether a portable three-channel EEG system (C3, Cz, C4) can decode successful versus unsuccessful futsal free-kicks from pre-movement activity. Linear SVMs decoded outcomes above chance within recording days, with selectively increased C3 beta-band power before successful kicks, but decoding did not generalize across days, indicating session-specific neural signatures.

papers.title: Neurophysiological Characterization of ADHD in Children Using EEG Signals: A Machine Learning Approach to Executive Function Networks.
papers.summary: Evaluated a subject-wise machine learning framework using multichannel EEG features to classify 61 children with ADHD versus 60 controls. Random Forest achieved the highest accuracy (0.8099), F1 (0.8160), and MCC (0.6204), with Fz contributing most, while individual alpha frequency-based band adjustment did not improve classification.

papers.title: Does Pre-Sensorimotor Brain Activity Modulate TMS-Evoked Potentials?
papers.summary: In 30 healthy participants performing kinesthetic motor imagery during single-pulse TMS over left primary motor cortex with 64-channel EEG, instructed left- and right-hand imagery produced similar mu/beta ERD and no reliable differences in TMS-evoked potentials; however, exploratory trial-by-trial analysis found overall effects of pre-stimulus brain state on TEP amplitudes, and greater pre-stimulus beta ERD correlated with larger P60 amplitudes.

papers.title: Critical Care Monitoring in Comatose Patients Receiving ECMO: A Cohort Study of Machine Learning on Quantitative EEG for Diagnosing Acute Brain Injury and Prognosticating Mortality.
papers.summary: Developed machine learning models on quantitative EEG and clinical variables to diagnose acute brain injury and prognosticate mortality in 57 comatose ECMO patients. qEEG-augmented models achieved an AUC of 0.769 for ABI detection versus 0.681 for clinical variables alone, and 0.864 for 30-day mortality, with frontal theta power and interhemispheric asymmetry as key features.

papers.title: Error Related Negativity and Error Positivity: Neural Indices of Double-Faults in Elite Athletes.
papers.summary: The study examined whether error-related negativity (ERN) and error positivity (Pe) amplitudes predict performance recovery after errors in a sport context versus a speeded laboratory task. In 15 professional basketball players, larger ERN and Pe amplitudes significantly predicted fewer consecutive missed free throws in the field (p < .001 and p = .017) but were not associated with the laboratory consecutive-error ratio.

papers.title: FUSE: FUsing EEG-MEG in a Shared Embedding via self-supervised learning for BCI
papers.summary: Introduces FUSE, a two-phase self-supervised framework that learns a shared EEG-MEG latent representation by predicting power spectral density from time-domain activity and then reuses the frozen encoder for motor imagery BCI classification. On simultaneous EEG-MEG from 20 participants, the learned representations raised median accuracy from 0.734 with handcrafted spectral features to 0.794, also outperforming MEG alone (0.680) and slightly EEG alone (0.765), with cross-subject transfer within 0.01 accuracy for over half of models.

papers.title: Montage-guided fusion network for long-term scalp electroencephalography seizure detection.
papers.summary: The authors propose MGF-Net, a montage-guided fusion network that represents fixed bipolar EEG derivations as nodes in a relation-labeled graph and uses a relation-aware graph Transformer for seizure detection; on CHB-MIT it achieved 98.38% segment-level accuracy and detected all 65 test seizure events with 100% sensitivity, 0.82/h false detection rate, and 2.03 s latency.

papers.title: MF-TopoNet: A Multi-Frequency Topological Neural Network for Epileptic Seizure Prediction.
papers.summary: The authors proposed MF-TopoNet, a multi-frequency topological neural network that combines functional brain networks and raw multi-channel EEG with a TopoConv module and cross-band attention for epileptic seizure prediction. Under 10-fold cross-validation, MF-TopoNet achieved 95.88% accuracy, 95.60% sensitivity, and 96.15% specificity on CHB-MIT, and 94.01% accuracy, 93.92% sensitivity, and 94.11% specificity on Siena.

papers.title: Beside Resting-State EEG in the Diagnosis and Prognosis of Patients with Disorders of Consciousness.
papers.summary: This study evaluated bedside resting-state EEG (rs-EEG) for diagnosing and prognosing disorders of consciousness in 207 patients using weekly 4-channel EEG and CRS-R assessments. Permutation entropy (PE) uniquely supported cross-sectional grading, longitudinal tracking, and prognosis, while other EEG features had limited or unstable utility; subtype-specific prognostic signatures were identified.

papers.title: Spectral and Directed Connectivity EEG Markers for Classifying Alzheimer's Disease, Frontotemporal Dementia, and Healthy Controls with Exploratory Photobiomodulation Case-Study Projection.
papers.summary: The study assessed whether spectral and Granger-causality-based directed connectivity EEG markers can classify Alzheimer's disease (AD), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and healthy controls (HC) using resting-state EEG from 88 participants. The spectral-only model achieved balanced accuracy 0.572 for three-class classification, while the combined GC+spectral model reached 0.710 for dementia vs. HC and 0.584 for AD vs. FTD; an exploratory photobiomodulation case showed longitudinal EEG reorganization.

papers.title: Optimized Efficient Channel Attention-based ShuffleNet Framework for EEG Graph-Based Brain Topology Modeling in Motor Imagery Tasks.
papers.summary: The paper develops ODL-BTMIT, a graph-based motor imagery EEG classification framework that extracts node degree and hybrid weighted node centrality topological features and classifies them with an Efficient Channel Attention-based ShuffleNet fine-tuned by Self-Improved Red Panda Optimization; it reported up to 96.6% accuracy and outperformed several existing methods in mean, median, and maximum accuracy.

papers.title: Quadratic and adaptive computations yield an efficient representation of song in Drosophila auditory receptor neurons
papers.summary: Combining electrophysiology and computational modeling, this study shows that a quadratic filter followed by divisive normalization accurately reproduces Drosophila auditory receptor neuron responses to artificial and natural sounds. These computations localize adaptive temporal filtering to antennal mechanics and variance adaptation to divisive normalization, producing a robust, easily decoded representation of courtship song despite ambiguity for arbitrary broadband stimuli.

papers.title: Motor Imagery Acquisition and Classification Using a Low-Cost 8-Channel EEG System in a VR ADHD Serious Game Environment: A Case Study.
papers.summary: This case study integrated a low-cost 8-channel OpenBCI Cyton EEG system into a VR serious game to acquire and classify motor imagery and concentration signals in an ADHD context. Under stable signal conditions, a subject-specific online classification accuracy of up to 90% was achieved with the EEGNet deep learning model, though high impedance, channel railing, and motion artifacts required mitigation.

papers.title: From signal to construct evidence: multimodal consumer-wearable sensing in real general-aviation flight.
papers.summary: In 40 pilots flying standardized maneuvers in a Cessna 172, multimodal wearable signals were assessed in nested evidence tiers; cardiac and oculomotor channels showed the strongest within-person convergence, but criterion-related frontal theta/alpha associations did not survive resampling and sensor features did not exceed a maneuver-only baseline in held-out pilots.

papers.title: Intensive Home-Based Motor Imagery Neurofeedback Training Using Mobile EEG to Assess Changes in Brain Activity and Motor Function in Stroke Survivors: A Multiple Baseline Design (MINTS Study Protocol)
papers.summary: This protocol describes a prospective, single-group, multiple-baseline study to investigate intensive home-based motor imagery neurofeedback training using mobile EEG in 21 chronic stroke survivors with upper-limb impairment. The study will assess changes in resting-state EEG coherence and MI-related EEG activity as primary outcomes, with secondary measures including fMRI, clinical motor outcomes, and movement sensors.

papers.title: A Wearable Multimodal Assistive Interface for Virtual Cursor Control in Stroke Survivors with Upper-Limb Impairment.
papers.summary: This study developed a wearable multimodal assistive interface using EOG, EEG, and IMU signals from a headband to enable virtual cursor control in stroke survivors with upper-limb impairment. In 30 patients, the system achieved 87.53% average accuracy, 3.49 s operation time, and 62.04 bits/min information transfer rate in a spelling task, with moderate NASA-TLX workload.

papers.title: BRAINet: A brain-region-aware interaction network for EEG-based diagnosis of disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: BRAINet, a brain-region-aware EEG framework, partitions channels into five anatomical regions, extracts region-specific spatiotemporal and spectral features, and models cross-region interactions with a Transformer for three-class DOC classification; on resting-state EEG from 22 UWS, 24 MCS-, and 15 MCS+ patients it achieved mean balanced accuracy of 54.07% at epoch level and 59.89% at subject level, significantly higher than the best baseline Conformer.

papers.title: EEG vs. Hybrid EEG-fNIRS BCI for FES Control in Healthy Subjects: A Blind Randomized Study and an Open Dataset.
papers.summary: A blind randomized study compared hybrid EEG-fNIRS versus EEG-only brain-computer interface control of functional electrical stimulation in 16 healthy volunteers over five sessions, finding no significant between-group differences in classification accuracy or sense of agency. Median three-class recall was 53.5% for hybrid and 57.3% for EEG-only, and the full dataset was released via NITRC.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Biomarkers for Early Detection and Monitoring of Neurological Disorders: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on artificial intelligence and digital biomarkers from eye tracking, speech, wearables, and passive sensing for early detection of neurological disorders. It emphasizes that most reported performance metrics derive from retrospective or internally validated datasets, so results should be considered proof-of-concept rather than clinically ready.

papers.title: Altered resting-state EEG microstate topographies and transition dynamics in generalized anxiety disorder.
papers.summary: Compared resting-state EEG microstate features between 104 patients with generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) and 89 healthy controls, finding topographic differences in MS-A, MS-D, and MS-E and reduced bidirectional transition probabilities between MS-B and MS-C in GAD after correction. Machine learning using microstate-derived features showed limited out-of-sample generalizability.

papers.title: KTU-MEDAFE: A Newly Developed Multimodal Dataset for Emotion Recognition Using EEG-Speech Decision-Level Fusion.
papers.summary: The study introduces KTU-MEDAFE, a multimodal dataset of synchronized EEG, speech, and facial videos from 40 participants, and evaluates EEG-speech decision-level fusion for binary emotion recognition using Angle-Amplitude Graph representations with ResNet-50 and GoogLeNet. Multimodal fusion achieved higher average classification performance than unimodal EEG or speech models, with substantial subject-dependent variability.

papers.title: [Research status and prospects of electroencephalogram characteristics in acupuncture for cognitive dysfunction].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.summary: Reviews recent EEG studies on acupuncture for cognitive dysfunction, summarizing evidence that acupuncture modulates abnormal brain electrical rhythms, improves microstate dynamics, and enhances functional connectivity in cognition-related brain regions. Discusses EEG's potential for identifying cognitive dysfunction stages and developing personalized acupuncture protocols.

papers.title: The Caffeinated Brain Part 3: The Effect of Caffeine on Electroencephalography (EEG) During Wakefulness-A Systematic and Mechanistic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized 48 studies on the effects of acute and habitual caffeine exposure on wakeful EEG measures, finding that reduced alpha power and attenuation of slow-frequency activity under sleep pressure or withdrawal were among the more frequently reported effects, but substantial methodological heterogeneity limits a single reproducible EEG signature. The evidence does not support EEG as a validated biomarker of caffeine response or improved cognitive performance.

papers.title: Students' Learning Engagement Detection Based on Cognition and Emotion Features: Improved Linknet-Squeezenet Architecture-Based Emotion Recognition.
papers.journal: International journal of developmental neuroscience : the official journal of the International Society for Developmental Neuroscience
papers.summary: Proposes an EEG-based student engagement detection framework using cognition and emotion features, with an improved LinkNet-SqueezeNet hybrid model. The model achieved a mean performance value of 0.954, outperforming several existing methods.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Rheumatology and Systemic Inflammatory Diseases: From Pattern Recognition to Signal Analysis and Clinical Decision Support.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes current and emerging applications of AI and ML in rheumatology and systemic inflammatory diseases, covering deep learning image analysis, NLP of electronic health records, multi-omic biomarker discovery, and Fourier transform-based signal processing for continuous disease monitoring. It also addresses challenges such as large language model hallucination and argues that AI expands what is observable, with epistemological implications for clinical knowledge.

papers.title: Postoperative delirium in ambulatory patients.
papers.summary: This review provides a mechanistic and pragmatic framework for postoperative delirium in ambulatory patients, noting that while POD occurs in <2% of ambulatory cases, detection is limited once patients are home. It proposes caregiver-based screening using the Family Confusion Assessment Method and discusses preventive strategies including multimodal prehabilitation, EEG-guided anesthesia, and family-delivered programs, which reduced POD incidence from 19.4% to 2.6% in one program (t-HELP).

papers.title: International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology standardized stereo-electroencephalography terminology.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Presents standardized stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) terminology developed through an international modified Delphi consensus process by 41 experts. The glossary defines background activities, interictal and ictal patterns, stimulation responses, and artifacts to promote consistent interpretation and multicenter collaboration in presurgical epilepsy evaluation.

papers.title: Towards continuous brain monitoring: a pilot qualitative study of user experiences with in-ear EEG.
papers.summary: This pilot qualitative study explored user experiences of in-ear EEG through semi-structured interviews with 10 participants, identifying five themes: embodied acceptability, pragmatic usability, reframing EEG as personal technology, conditional adoption, and future integration. Participants found the device comfortable and unobtrusive, comparing it to earbuds, but adoption was conditional on demonstrating clinical accuracy comparable to traditional EEG.

papers.title: EEG changes associated with stress reduction in university students following exposure to essential oil odors.
papers.summary: Investigated EEG changes in 33 university students after inhalation of six essential oils, finding increased relative alpha power and decreased beta power, with significant increases in alpha-to-beta ratio for lavender, tea tree, chamomile, and rosemary. Connectivity patterns showed regional redistribution, and relative alpha activity was highest in the parietal region.

papers.title: Chronic Stress Induces Retinal Ganglion Cell Degeneration Featuring Reduced Density, Altered Intrinsic Electrophysiology, and Light Responses.
papers.summary: Using a mouse model of chronic unpredictable stress, this study found reduced blood perfusion in the retinal inner plexiform layer, decreased retinal ganglion cell density (with greater loss of ipRGCs), and altered intrinsic electrophysiological properties of surviving RGCs, including decreased membrane input resistance and increased stimulus-size-dependent light responses. The results suggest retinal layer- and RGC-type-specific susceptibilities in depression.

papers.title: Systemic inflammatory profiles associated with early EEG abnormalities following ischemic stroke: a cohort study.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 307 acute supratentorial ischemic stroke patients with EEG within 72 h, elevated neutrophil count was independently associated with early epileptiform discharges (OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.05–1.36) and improved model discrimination, while no inflammatory biomarker independently predicted slow-wave activity after adjustment.

papers.title: A Review of the Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Cardiac Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes contemporary artificial intelligence applications in cardiac electrophysiology, covering arrhythmia detection, catheter ablation, cardiac implantable electronic devices, and AI-enhanced ECG. It reports that deep neural networks classify rhythms comparably to cardiologists on internal test sets, identify occult atrial fibrillation from normal sinus-rhythm ECG, and an AI algorithm adjudicating intracardiac electrogram dispersion improved single-procedure freedom from atrial fibrillation in a randomized trial of persistent atrial fibrillation.

papers.title: Transient Postoperative Myoclonus Following Hypothermic Circulatory Arrest.
papers.summary: A 72-year-old man developed transient bilateral myoclonus, diffuse rigidity, and suspected eyelid apraxia after ascending aorta and hemiarch replacement under hypothermic circulatory arrest; symptoms resolved by postoperative day 3 with levetiracetam and calcium supplementation, and he was discharged neurologically intact.

papers.title: Electrophysiology Laboratory Survival Guide Part 2: Introduction to Intracardiac Echocardiography in the Electrophysiology Laboratory.
papers.summary: This review provides an introduction to intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) in the electrophysiology laboratory, describing the catheter-based ultrasound probe, image orientation, and standard views. It explains that ICE requires additional vascular access but provides real-time intracardiac analysis, with the home view having the catheter in the right atrium facing the tricuspid valve and additional views obtained by clockwise rotation.

papers.title: Fahr syndrome in an 18-year-old male with pseudohypoparathyroidism: Clinical-radiological dissociation.
papers.summary: An 18-year-old male with pseudohypoparathyroidism and medication non-compliance presented with headaches, carpopedal spasms, and depressed mood, with extensive bilateral intracranial calcifications on CT/MRI but largely unremarkable neurological examination; calcium and calcitriol optimization resolved spasms and improved symptoms at 15 days.

papers.title: Electrophysiology Laboratory Survival Guide Part 1: Electrogram Basics, Catheters, and Basic Intervals.
papers.summary: This review covers the basics of cardiac electrograms (EGMs), electrophysiology catheters, and basic intervals measured in the EP laboratory. It explains that EGMs represent electrical potentials within the immediate vicinity of catheters placed in the right atrium, right ventricle, coronary sinus, and near the His bundle, and when used with a surface ECG, they allow study of timing of electrical activity and arrhythmias.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
